title.zh: 把整体描述与一个局部分开说
title.en: Describe the arrangement and one local feature separately

paragraphs.zh: 回看上面的第一张原创图，先用一句话描述两侧形状与中间白隙的关系，再挑一个小点或凸起另写一句。两句话可以同时成立，无需决定哪一种看法更高级。若别人想从局部开始，可以听听他指的是哪里，再回到整张图。只描述看得到的安排即可，不必给墨迹取一个物体名称。复盘不测全局能力，也不要求以后每张图都先看整体。
paragraphs.en: Revisit the first original image and describe the relationship between the two forms and central white gap in one sentence. Give a nearby dot or projection a separate sentence. Both can stand without ranking the approaches. If someone begins locally, hear which part they mean before returning to the arrangement. No object name is needed. This describes visible features without measuring big-picture ability or requiring the same starting point for every image.

title.zh: 围绕同一处图像交换看法
title.en: Discuss the same part of an image

paragraphs.zh: 可以问：“假设先描述这张图的两侧和白隙，你会怎样说？别人又想从哪个局部开始？”比较的是这张原创图前的描述与选择，不是分析对方是什么样的人。
paragraphs.en: Ask: “How would you describe the two sides and white gap first, and which local feature might someone else begin with?” Compare descriptions and choices about this original image rather than analyse what kind of person someone is.

paragraphs.zh: 可以只分享这份公开说明，链接不含本次答案或计数。对方可以不回答、不继续看图，也不必上传个人图像或讲述私人联想。

title.zh: 让一个小细节有可指明的位置
title.en: Give a small detail a location others can identify

paragraphs.zh: 沿用上面的第七张原创图，挑一段白隙旁的弯折，用左或右、上或下来说明位置。再看看自己想沿边继续，还是转去比较附近色块。两种选择不互相否定，也不需要找齐所有差异。若与同伴交流，先确认双方说的是同一位置；对方没有兴趣时可以结束。复盘让描述更具体，不把发现多少细节当成认真程度、视力或分析能力的成绩。
paragraphs.en: For the seventh original image, choose a bend beside the white gap and locate it by side and height. Decide whether to follow the edge or compare a nearby colour region instead. Neither choice cancels the other, and finding every difference is unnecessary. With a companion, first check that you mean the same location; the exchange can end if they are uninterested. Make a description specific without counting details as a grade for effort, vision or analysis.

title.zh: 围绕同一处图像交换看法
title.en: Discuss the same part of an image

paragraphs.zh: 可以问：“假设想让朋友找到你正在说的一段边缘，你会用哪些位置词，而不是先替它解释含义？”比较的是这张原创图前的描述与选择，不是分析对方是什么样的人。
paragraphs.en: Ask: “If you wanted a friend to locate the edge you meant, which position words would you use before assigning it a meaning?” Compare descriptions and choices about this original image rather than analyse what kind of person someone is.

title.zh: 把静止形状与想象的变化分开
title.en: Separate the static form from an imagined change

paragraphs.zh: 回到上面的第三张原创图，先指出一个实际可见的轮廓，再另说你想象它怎样展开或收拢。可以用“如果它动起来，我会想到……”开头，明确变化来自联想，图本身仍是静止的。另一个人可能想到相反方向，也可能完全不想到运动；这些都不需要纠正。复盘只让联想有明确参照，不由此判断行动快慢、身体状态或想象力高低。
paragraphs.en: Return to the third original image and identify one visible contour before describing an imagined opening or gathering. You might begin, “If it moved, I would imagine…” to keep the change separate from the static image. Another person may imagine the opposite direction or no movement at all; neither needs correction. Give an association a reference without inferring speed of action, bodily state or a level of imagination.

title.zh: 围绕同一处图像交换看法
title.en: Discuss the same part of an image

paragraphs.zh: 可以问：“假设这条静止轮廓可以有一种想象中的变化，你会想到哪个方向，又怎样说明它其实没有移动？”比较的是这张原创图前的描述与选择，不是分析对方是什么样的人。
paragraphs.en: Ask: “If this static contour suggested an imagined change, which direction would you picture and how would you distinguish it from actual movement?” Compare descriptions and choices about this original image rather than analyse what kind of person someone is.

title.zh: 比较两个色块，不为颜色分配性格
title.en: Compare two colour regions without assigning character

paragraphs.zh: 沿用上面的第四张原创图，选外层与内斑两个区域，描述它们在你当前屏幕上的深浅、大小或相邻关系。喜欢哪种颜色可以另说，不用把偏好当成情绪或人格密码。若同伴看到的颜色不同，先保留屏幕和观看条件的差异，而不是判断谁看得更准确。也可以只读结构说明或停止观看；复盘不要求训练色觉、改变心情或证明审美。
paragraphs.en: For the fourth original image, compare an outer region and an inner patch by their darkness, size or adjacency on your current display. Colour liking can be a separate comment rather than a code for emotion or personality. If a companion sees different colours, retain differences in displays and viewing conditions without deciding who sees more accurately. Reading the structural description or stopping is also possible; no colour-vision training, mood change or aesthetic proof is required.

title.zh: 围绕同一处图像交换看法
title.en: Discuss the same part of an image

paragraphs.zh: 可以问：“假设比较外层和内斑，你会先说深浅、大小，还是相邻关系？这与你喜欢哪种颜色有什么不同？”比较的是这张原创图前的描述与选择，不是分析对方是什么样的人。
paragraphs.en: Ask: “When comparing the outer form and inner patch, would you begin with darkness, size or adjacency, and how does that differ from liking a colour?” Compare descriptions and choices about this original image rather than analyse what kind of person someone is.

title.zh: 给临时场景加上“此刻的联想”
title.en: Name the scene as a present association

paragraphs.zh: 回看上面的第五张原创图，先指出一处形状，再说它此刻可以让你联想到怎样的小场景。例如，把中间白隙暂时想成入口，不等于图里藏有一个作者规定的答案。可以只留一句、换一种联想或没有场景。若愿意分享，只讲想讲的部分；不需要解释私人记忆或证明故事完整。复盘区分可见形状与自己补出的画面，不把它们当作无意识内容的证据。
paragraphs.en: Revisit the fifth original image, identify a shape and describe a small scene it might suggest now. Temporarily treating the white gap as an entrance supplies no hidden answer set by the author. Keep one sentence, change the association or imagine no scene. Share only what you want without explaining private memories or completing a story. Separate the visible shape from the picture you add rather than treat either as evidence of unconscious content.

title.zh: 围绕同一处图像交换看法
title.en: Discuss the same part of an image

paragraphs.zh: 可以问：“假设把白隙暂时想成一个入口，图上实际有什么，哪些部分是你此刻加上的联想？”比较的是这张原创图前的描述与选择，不是分析对方是什么样的人。
paragraphs.en: Ask: “If you temporarily imagined the white gap as an entrance, what would actually be visible and which parts would be your association?” Compare descriptions and choices about this original image rather than analyse what kind of person someone is.
